## Overview

This notebook performs **Step 5** of the analysis: it groups cells using their
principal-component (PCA) coordinates, summarizes marker expression for each
cluster, and adds optional manual cell-type labels. Clusters are exploratory
groups, not automatically discovered biological cell types; inspect their
marker profiles and validate labels against domain knowledge before interpreting
them.

Inputs from Step 4:

- `results/sce_dimensionality_reduced.rds`

Outputs from this notebook:

- `results/clustering_summary/clustering_parameters.csv`
- `results/clustering_summary/cluster_sizes.csv`
- `results/clustering_summary/marker_means_by_cluster.csv`
- `results/clustering_summary/cluster_annotation_template.csv`
- `results/sce_clustered_annotated.rds`

The annotation template is created on the first render. Review the per-cluster
marker means, fill in the template's `annotation` column with cell-type labels,
then render this notebook again to save those labels with the cells.

## Load the PCA and UMAP object

```{r load-sce}
# Step 4 saves both the original cell data and reduced dimensions in this object.
sce_path <- file.path("..", "results", "sce_dimensionality_reduced.rds")
if (!file.exists(sce_path)) {
  stop("Missing results/sce_dimensionality_reduced.rds. Please render notebooks/04_dimensionality_reduction.qmd first.")
}

# Loading the saved object preserves the exact cell order for clustering and
# writing cluster labels back into colData.
sce_clustered <- readRDS(sce_path)

# Verify the expected PCA embedding exists and has at least two dimensions.
if (!"PCA" %in% reducedDimNames(sce_clustered)) {
  stop("The input object does not contain a PCA reduced dimension.")
}
pca_embedding <- reducedDim(sce_clustered, "PCA")
if (ncol(pca_embedding) < 2L) {
  stop("PCA must contain at least two components to cluster and visualize cells.")
}

# Show the object and its available embeddings for an initial sanity check.
cat("Cells:", ncol(sce_clustered), "\n")
cat("Markers:", nrow(sce_clustered), "\n")
cat("Reduced dimensions:", paste(reducedDimNames(sce_clustered), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

---

## Configure clustering

We use base R's k-means algorithm on the leading PCA coordinates. PCA provides a
compact representation of correlated marker measurements, while avoiding the
common mistake of treating the two-dimensional UMAP layout as a quantitative
distance space. UMAP is used below only to visualize the resulting labels.

The number of clusters and number of PCs are analysis choices, not universal
truths. Change them below, compare alternative settings, and inspect cluster
sizes and marker profiles. The chosen values and random seed are recorded in the
output parameter table.

```{r clustering-configuration}
# Number of clusters to estimate; adjust after exploring cluster diagnostics.
n_clusters <- 20L
# Use up to the first 15 PCs, or fewer if Step 4 produced fewer components.
n_pcs_for_clustering <- min(15L, ncol(pca_embedding))
# Fix the seed so repeated renders with the same inputs and settings are stable.
clustering_seed <- 2026L
# Multiple starts reduce dependence on one random initialization.
kmeans_nstart <- 5L
# Limit iteration count while allowing ordinary datasets to converge.
kmeans_iter_max <- 100L

# Guard against invalid settings before starting a potentially expensive fit.
if (nrow(pca_embedding) <= n_clusters) {
  stop("The number of cells must be greater than n_clusters.")
}
if (n_clusters < 2L) {
  stop("n_clusters must be at least 2.")
}

# Extract only the selected leading PCs to bound clustering memory and runtime.
pca_for_clustering <- pca_embedding[, seq_len(n_pcs_for_clustering), drop = FALSE]
if (any(!is.finite(pca_for_clustering))) {
  stop("The selected PCA coordinates contain missing or non-finite values.")
}

cat("Clustering", nrow(pca_for_clustering), "cells using",
    ncol(pca_for_clustering), "PCs into", n_clusters, "clusters.\n")
```

---

## Cluster cells in PCA space

```{r run-clustering}
# Seed k-means to make its random starting centers reproducible.
set.seed(clustering_seed)

# Treat each row as one cell and each selected PC as a clustering feature.
kmeans_fit <- stats::kmeans(
  x = pca_for_clustering,
  centers = n_clusters,
  iter.max = kmeans_iter_max,
  nstart = kmeans_nstart,
  algorithm = "Lloyd"
)

# Give cluster IDs stable, readable names for tables, plots, and colData.
cluster_levels <- sprintf("Cluster_%02d", seq_len(n_clusters))
cluster_id <- factor(
  cluster_levels[kmeans_fit$cluster],
  levels = cluster_levels
)

# Store one cluster ID per cell in the SCE so downstream steps can reuse it.
colData(sce_clustered)$cluster_id <- cluster_id

# Summarize cell counts, including any empty levels for a complete cluster list.
cluster_sizes <- as.data.frame(table(cluster_id), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(cluster_sizes) <- c("cluster_id", "n_cells")
cluster_sizes$percent_cells <- 100 * cluster_sizes$n_cells / ncol(sce_clustered)
cluster_sizes
```

```{r fig-cluster-sizes}
#| fig-cap: "Number of cells assigned to each PCA-space cluster."
# Plot cluster sizes to make highly imbalanced or unexpectedly small groups visible.
ggplot(cluster_sizes, aes(x = cluster_id, y = n_cells)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Cells per cluster",
    x = "Cluster",
    y = "Number of cells"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Visualize clusters on the embeddings

```{r fig-clusters-pca}
#| fig-cap: "PCA embedding coloured by the k-means cluster assignments."
# Plot the first two PCA axes; this is a diagnostic view, not the full clustering space.
pca_plot_df <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_embedding[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_embedding[, 2],
  cluster_id = cluster_id
)

ggplot(pca_plot_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = cluster_id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 0.6) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA embedding by cluster",
    subtitle = sprintf("Clustering used the first %d PCs", n_pcs_for_clustering),
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2",
    colour = "Cluster"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig-clusters-umap}
#| fig-cap: "UMAP embedding coloured by the PCA-space cluster assignments, when available."
# UMAP can show neighborhood structure, but its axes and distances are not used
# to compute the k-means clusters.
if ("UMAP" %in% reducedDimNames(sce_clustered)) {
  umap_embedding <- reducedDim(sce_clustered, "UMAP")
  if (ncol(umap_embedding) >= 2L) {
    umap_plot_df <- data.frame(
      UMAP1 = umap_embedding[, 1],
      UMAP2 = umap_embedding[, 2],
      cluster_id = cluster_id
    )

    ggplot(umap_plot_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, colour = cluster_id)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 0.6) +
      labs(
        title = "UMAP embedding by cluster",
        x = "UMAP1",
        y = "UMAP2",
        colour = "Cluster"
      ) +
      theme_bw()
  } else {
    plot.new()
    text(0.5, 0.5, "UMAP is present but has fewer than two dimensions.")
  }
} else {
  # Keep the document informative when the optional UMAP calculation failed upstream.
  plot.new()
  text(0.5, 0.5, "UMAP was not computed in Step 4; PCA clustering is still available.")
}
```

## Summarize marker expression by cluster

Marker expression profiles help guide biological interpretation of each cluster.
The summary below reports mean values in the preprocessing assay (for example,
asinh-transformed expression). It is a descriptive aid, not an automatic
cell-type classifier; marker combinations and relevant biological context should
be considered when assigning labels.

```{r marker-profiles}
# Reuse the assay selected in preprocessing whenever that metadata is available.
analysis_assay <- metadata(sce_clustered)$preprocessing$analysis_assay
if (is.null(analysis_assay) || !analysis_assay %in% assayNames(sce_clustered)) {
  # For older or externally produced objects, use a familiar expression assay.
  assay_candidates <- c("exprs", "quant_norm", "counts", "scaled")
  available_candidates <- assay_candidates[assay_candidates %in% assayNames(sce_clustered)]
  if (length(available_candidates) == 0L) {
    stop("No supported assay is available for cluster marker summaries.")
  }
  analysis_assay <- available_candidates[1]
}

# Calculate each cluster's marker means separately to avoid materializing an
# additional full cell-by-marker copy of the assay.
cluster_marker_means <- vapply(cluster_levels, function(current_cluster) {
  cells_in_cluster <- which(cluster_id == current_cluster)
  rowMeans(
    assay(sce_clustered, analysis_assay)[, cells_in_cluster, drop = FALSE],
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}, numeric(nrow(sce_clustered)))

# Keep marker names explicit in the exported wide table for easy review.
cluster_marker_means <- as.data.frame(cluster_marker_means, check.names = FALSE)
cluster_marker_means$marker <- rownames(sce_clustered)
cluster_marker_means <- cluster_marker_means[
  , c("marker", cluster_levels), drop = FALSE
]

cat("Marker means use the", analysis_assay, "assay.\n")
head(cluster_marker_means)
```

---

## Review and add manual annotations

The exported template keeps annotation separate from the unsupervised cluster
IDs. Fill in the `annotation` column only after reviewing the corresponding
marker means and plots. Leave a cell blank if the cluster is unresolved; blanks
are stored as missing values rather than presented as confirmed cell types.

```{r manual-annotations}
# Keep the template aligned to current cluster IDs while retaining labels that
# match clusters from an earlier render.
annotation_path <- file.path(
  "..", "results", "clustering_summary", "cluster_annotation_template.csv"
)
annotation_template <- data.frame(
  cluster_id = cluster_levels,
  annotation = rep("", length(cluster_levels)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

if (file.exists(annotation_path)) {
  # Read the user's edited table without converting labels to factors.
  saved_annotations <- read.csv(
    annotation_path,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  # Validate the hand-edited file so invalid labels cannot silently misalign.
  required_columns <- c("cluster_id", "annotation")
  if (!all(required_columns %in% names(saved_annotations))) {
    stop("Annotation template must contain cluster_id and annotation columns.")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(saved_annotations$cluster_id)) {
    stop("Annotation template contains duplicate cluster_id values.")
  }

  # Carry forward annotations for cluster IDs that still exist; new clusters
  # remain blank and obsolete IDs are dropped from the refreshed template.
  annotation_match <- match(annotation_template$cluster_id, saved_annotations$cluster_id)
  existing_labels <- trimws(as.character(saved_annotations$annotation[annotation_match]))
  existing_labels[is.na(existing_labels)] <- ""
  annotation_template$annotation <- existing_labels
}

# Refresh the template after reconciling it with this run's cluster IDs. Users
# can edit this CSV and render again to include their annotations in the SCE.
write.csv(annotation_template, annotation_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "")

# Match one reviewed label to every cell by its cluster ID.
cell_annotations <- annotation_template$annotation[
  match(as.character(cluster_id), annotation_template$cluster_id)
]
cell_annotations <- trimws(cell_annotations)
cell_annotations[cell_annotations == ""] <- NA_character_
colData(sce_clustered)$cluster_annotation <- cell_annotations

# Show annotation coverage so blank labels are not mistaken for completed work.
cat("Clusters with annotations:",
    sum(nzchar(annotation_template$annotation)), "of", n_clusters, "\n")
annotation_template
```

## Save outputs

```{r save-outputs}
# Save run settings and fit diagnostics so the analysis can be reproduced.
clustering_parameters <- data.frame(
  parameter = c(
    "method",
    "n_cells",
    "n_clusters",
    "n_pcs_used",
    "assay_for_marker_means",
    "seed",
    "nstart",
    "iter_max",
    "iterations_used",
    "total_within_cluster_sum_of_squares"
  ),
  value = c(
    "k-means on PCA coordinates",
    as.character(ncol(sce_clustered)),
    as.character(n_clusters),
    as.character(n_pcs_for_clustering),
    analysis_assay,
    as.character(clustering_seed),
    as.character(kmeans_nstart),
    as.character(kmeans_iter_max),
    as.character(kmeans_fit$iter),
    as.character(kmeans_fit$tot.withinss)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Export tables that support independent review of the clustering and labels.
write.csv(
  clustering_parameters,
  file.path("..", "results", "clustering_summary", "clustering_parameters.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(
  cluster_sizes,
  file.path("..", "results", "clustering_summary", "cluster_sizes.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(
  cluster_marker_means,
  file.path("..", "results", "clustering_summary", "marker_means_by_cluster.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Save the annotated object; blank manual labels remain NA in colData.
saveRDS(
  sce_clustered,
  file = file.path("..", "results", "sce_clustered_annotated.rds")
)

# List files written so the handoff to downstream analysis is explicit.
cat("Saved:\n")
cat("  results/clustering_summary/clustering_parameters.csv\n")
cat("  results/clustering_summary/cluster_sizes.csv\n")
cat("  results/clustering_summary/marker_means_by_cluster.csv\n")
cat("  results/clustering_summary/cluster_annotation_template.csv\n")
cat("  results/sce_clustered_annotated.rds\n")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Interpretation and next step

Cluster IDs represent data-driven groups, while `cluster_annotation` contains
only labels entered in the annotation template. Revisit the chosen cluster
number and PC count if groups are too broad, too small, or difficult to
interpret. Downstream analyses can load `results/sce_clustered_annotated.rds`
and use both columns in `colData`.
:::
